  "request": "Add a `remove` command to the demo todo CLI (examples/demo) so a user can delete an item by id: `todo remove <id>` prints `removed <id>` and the item no longer appears in `todo list`; for an unknown id it must exit non-zero with the message `no item <id>`.",
  "has_zones": true

acceptance: Running `todo remove <id>` with an existing id prints exactly `removed <id>` and exits zero.
After `todo remove <id>` succeeds, that item no longer appears in the output of `todo list`.
Running `todo remove <id>` with an unknown id prints the message `no item <id>`.
For an unknown id, `todo remove <id>` exits with a non-zero status.
The `remove` command lives in the demo todo CLI under examples/demo, alongside the existing commands.
Existing commands (e.g. `todo list`) keep working as before after the change.

acceptance.text: WHEN the user runs `todo remove <id>` and an item with that id exists THE SYSTEM SHALL print `removed <id>` on stdout and exit with status 0.
WHEN the user runs `todo list` after a successful `todo remove <id>` THE SYSTEM SHALL show no line for that id while every other item still appears exactly as before.
WHEN the user runs `todo remove <id>` and no item with that id exists THE SYSTEM SHALL print `no item <id>` and exit with a non-zero status.
WHEN `todo remove <id>` fails with `no item <id>` THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the output of `todo list` identical to what it was before the attempt.
WHEN the user runs `todo remove <id>` for an item already marked done THE SYSTEM SHALL remove it the same way as an open item.
WHEN the user runs `todo add`, `todo done` or `todo list` after a `todo remove` THE SYSTEM SHALL keep working on the saved file exactly as before.
WHEN the user runs `todo` with an unknown command THE SYSTEM SHALL print a usage line that mentions `todo remove <id>`.
(internal) WHEN `cd examples/demo && npm test` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass, including a test that removes a known id and one that rejects an unknown id with `no item <id>`.

questions.text: What should `todo remove` do when no id is given at all?
questions.default: Mirror the existing `todo done`: any id that matches no item, including a missing one, is reported as `no item <id>` with a non-zero exit.
questions.why: Only affects an edge case outside the request; the default is consistent with current behaviour and needs no new rule.

questions.text: After removing the item with the highest id, may `todo add` reuse that id?
questions.default: Keep the current id assignment unchanged (max+1), so reuse is possible; ids are not promised to be unique over time.
questions.why: Changing id allocation would touch add and the file format; nothing in the request asks for it.

questions.text: Should removing an item that is already done be allowed?
questions.default: Yes: any existing id can be removed, done or open.
questions.why: The request says 'delete an item by id' without restriction; refusing would need a second error message it does not define.

extra: A4: failed remove leaves `todo list` output unchanged
A5: removing a done item works the same as an open item
A7: usage line for unknown command mentions `todo remove <id>`
A8: npm test in examples/demo passes with remove tests (internal)
